content: Mefloquine Hydrochloride Tablets USP are a pharmaceutical formulation used as an antimalarial agent. Each tablet contains 250 mg of mefloquine hydrochloride, which is chemically equivalent to 228 mg of the free base form of the drug. This medication is intended for oral administration. Mefloquine Hydrochloride USP is a derivative of 4-quinolinemethanol and is chemically named (R, S)-(±)-α-2-piperidinyl-2,8-bis(trifluoromethyl)-4-quinolinemethanol hydrochloride. Structurally, it is a 2-aryl substituted analog of quinine, a compound historically used to treat malaria. The drug appears as a white to nearly white crystalline substance and is only slightly soluble in water. The inactive components of the tablet formulation include colloidal silicon dioxide, corn starch, crospovidone, lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, pregelatinized starch, poloxamer, and talc. These excipients are included to aid in the manufacturing process, stability, and bioavailability of the medication.
